sentences.text:
(Presently Lodged In Dist. Jail, Barmer)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Girdhar Singh Bhati
For Respondent(s) : Mr. N.S. Chandawat, PP  Mr. Vikram Singh Rathore for  complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJENDRA PRAKASH SONI Order 09/10/2024 1.
Petitioner is lugged and locked in F.I.R No.132/2024 of Police Station Shiv, District Barmer, for the offence under Section(s) 450 and 376 of the I.P.C.

He has filed this application for restoration of liberty under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of the old Code).
2.
Heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner, learned public prosecutor and carefully perused the entire material available on record.
3. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State has strongly objected the different submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner and craves rejection of the petitioner's bail application.

Learned counsel for the complainant has not disputed the fact of [2024:RJ-JD:41484] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-12264/2024] compromise and has expressed his no objection to the petitioner being released on bail.

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the rival submissions with reference to material placed before me.

5. On perusal of the record and upon consideration of the submissions, it would be clear that both the parties have reached at a settlement on some points and counsel for the complainant admits that compromise has been arrived at between the parties and he has no grievance, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail.
6. Having considered the material available on record; the arguments advanced by counsel for the petitioner particularly the facts narrated above and the fact that bail rejection order goes to show that petitioner is not involved in any other case.; that trial is likely to take its own considerable time and taking note of all these aspects, I do not intend to go into the merits of the matter but of the considered view that the petitioner has available to him substantial grounds so as to question the prosecution case and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioner in detention for an indefinite period therefore, I am inclined to grant indulgence of bail to the petitioner at this stage.
7.

Consequently, the present bail application is allowed and it is directed that the accused-petitioner Shyam Singh @ Sumer Singh, arrested in connection with the F.I.R. No.132/2024 of Police Station Shiv, District Barmer shall be released on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond and two surety bonds of sufficient amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing [2024:RJ-JD:41484] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12264/2024] and as and when called upon to do so.

This order is subject to the condition that accused, within 7 days of his release, and sureties on the day of furnishing bail, will also furnish details of their all bank accounts, with bank and branch name, in shape of an affidavit, and submit legible copy of their Aadhar cards as well as copy of front page of Bank pass book, for smooth recovery of penalty amount, if there arise a need for recovery of penalty under Section 446 Cr.P.C in future.
(RAJENDRA PRAKASH SONI),J 425-Payal/-
